facets.description: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 8-10, minimumTokenResponseSchema: the computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` become fixed junk strings, not wildcard keys. The schema then requires a key that does not exist, so it always fails in sync mode.
parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 25-26: when the response has no refresh_token, the literal 'refresh_token' placeholder is injected. Callers save it, overwriting the real refresh token.

answer.reasoning: I agree with Labeler 2. The line-8 and line-10 computed keys are one defect in one place. Both come from the same bad pattern, both sit in the same schema, and one edit fixes them: replace the schema with a passthrough schema and an explicit expiry field. Splitting them into two facets, as Labeler 1 did, would wrongly mark s_1e566d8d incomplete for naming only the line-8 key. Its fix (a passthrough schema) already handles the line-10 key. s_1e566d8d and s_b03866bc both clearly report the junk keys and the 'refresh_token' placeholder being saved over the real token. s_3c4702d6 talks only about the schema keys and comments and never mentions the placeholder.
